beats.label: S1 · The clinic reopens
beats.text: Otis, son of sex therapist Jean, teams up with rebellious Maeve to run an underground sex clinic at Moordale after a chlamydia scare shows how badly students need real advice.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the show's premise and the Otis-Maeve partnership at the core of the whole series.

beats.label: S1 · Blended families
beats.text: Otis starts dating classmate Ola just as her father Jakob confesses his relationship with Otis's mother Jean, and the two families begin awkwardly overlapping.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the blended household dynamics that dominate S2 when Jakob and Ola move into Jean's house.

beats.label: S1 · Too late
beats.text: Otis fumbles intimacy with Ola while burying feelings for Maeve; when Maeve finally confesses hers, Otis lashes out that she has left it too late.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Otis-Maeve romantic misfire that keeps them circling each other into S2.

beats.label: S1 · Adam and Eric
beats.text: Expelled from military school, Adam returns and secretly hooks up with Eric — the boy he used to bully — while Eric starts openly dating new student Rahim.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Adam-Eric bond that drives both characters' arcs into S2 and beyond.

beats.label: S1 · Erin returns
beats.text: Maeve's addict mother Erin arrives with her toddler sister Elsie, relapses, and swears never to forgive Maeve after social services take both of them away.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Erin's grievance becomes an active threat again when she kidnaps Elsie in S2.

beats.label: S1 · Aimee on the bus
beats.text: Aimee is sexually assaulted on the bus and slowly unravels; a shared detention with the other girls turns into a group effort to coax her back on.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Aimee's trauma becomes her main storyline in S2 through Jean's therapy.

beats.label: S1 · Musical night
beats.text: Groff pins Jean's therapy notes across school in revenge; at the school musical Adam declares his love for Eric, and Isaac deletes Otis's voicemail confessing his to Maeve.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The unheard voicemail is the specific unresolved lie that detonates early in S2.

cliffhanger.text: Otis has left Maeve a voicemail confessing everything, but Isaac deleted it before she heard it. Maeve believes Otis said nothing on the same night social services took her mother and toddler sister away.
questions: Will Maeve ever discover what Otis actually said in that voicemail?
Can she survive on her own now that Erin and Elsie are gone?
Who is Isaac really, if his very first move was to lie to her?

characters.name: Otis Milburn
characters.line: Awkward teen running the school sex clinic; secretly in love with Maeve, unaware his confession voicemail was deleted.

characters.name: Maeve Wiley
characters.line: Otis's tough, brilliant clinic partner; social services just took her mother and sister, and she thinks Otis never called.

characters.name: Eric Effiong
characters.line: Otis's best friend; publicly chose Adam after Adam's declaration at the musical, leaving Rahim heartbroken.

characters.name: Jean Milburn
characters.line: Otis's mother and a sex therapist; kissed Otis's dad Remi in a lapse and lost Jakob over it.

characters.name: Adam Groff
characters.line: Former bully back from military school; publicly declared his love for Eric after months of secret hookups.

characters.name: Michael Groff
characters.line: Sacked headmaster who exposed Jean's therapy notes around school; his wife has asked for a divorce.

characters.name: Aimee Gibbs
characters.line: Maeve's cheerful best friend; sexually assaulted on the bus, slowly recognising how deeply it has affected her.

characters.name: Isaac
characters.line: Maeve's new wheelchair-using neighbour who deleted Otis's confession voicemail before she heard it.

characters.name: Erin Wiley
characters.line: Maeve's addict mother; just lost custody of Elsie and vowed never to forgive Maeve for the call to social services.

characters.name: Jackson Marchetti
characters.line: Head boy who quit swimming after breaking his hand on purpose; found new confidence through the school musical.

beats.label: S2 · Hope arrives
beats.text: New head Hope Haddon vows to restore Moordale's reputation, and after Otis tips her off she demolishes the toilets that were housing the sex clinic.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Hope's regime redefines Moordale and directly triggers the school's collapse by season's end.

beats.label: S2 · Ruby's I love you
beats.text: Otis and Ruby slide from a secret hookup into a real relationship, but when she finally says she loves him he cannot say it back and she ends it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ruby's brief taste of Otis is the seed of their reappearance as a couple in S3.

beats.label: S2 · Aimee in therapy
beats.text: Aimee begins therapy with Jean over her bus assault; a detention with the other girls turns into a group confession that walks her back onto the bus.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Aimee's healing anchors her whole S2 storyline and reshapes her intimacy going forward.

beats.label: S2 · Paternity doubt
beats.text: Jean tells Jakob she is pregnant and they try to co-parent, but he finds another man's jewellery in her house and asks for a paternity test.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The paternity uncertainty is what pays off in the shocking cliffhanger read.

beats.label: S2 · The Somme kiss
beats.text: Isaac confesses he deleted Otis's old voicemail; later, on the Somme trip, Otis and Maeve finally kiss, and Maeve asks for time to think it through.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The kiss finally aligns Otis and Maeve, which is what makes Maeve's departure hurt in S3.

beats.label: S2 · Hope falls
beats.text: Non-binary newcomer Cal defies Hope's uniform crackdown; Viv secretly films Hope's contempt for students and, on open day, the video ends her career at Moordale.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains how Moordale unravels and introduces Cal, who anchors the S3 Cavendish arc.

beats.label: S2 · Everyone scatters
beats.text: Aimee talks Maeve into taking the American scholarship; Eric breaks up with Adam despite his poem; the school will be sold; and Jean's paternity result stuns her.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cascades every relationship into S3's new starting positions in a single beat.

cliffhanger.text: Maeve has flown to America the same day she and Otis finally chose each other, Moordale is being sold out from under everyone, and Jean has just read a paternity result too shocking to share.
questions: Can Otis and Maeve survive an ocean apart just as they finally got together?
Whose baby is Jean actually raising?
Where do the sex school's students even go now that it's being sold?

characters.name: Otis Milburn
characters.line: Newly single after failing to say he loved Ruby; finally kissed Maeve on the school trip only for her to fly to America.

characters.name: Maeve Wiley
characters.line: Left for the American gifted-writers programme just as she and Otis got together; her mother Erin briefly kidnapped Elsie from care.

characters.name: Eric Effiong
characters.line: Broke up with Adam, deciding he needs a partner comfortable being out; kissed a boy in Nigeria and confessed to Adam.

characters.name: Jean Milburn
characters.line: Gave birth to a girl and read a paternity test whose result stunned her; Jakob does not know yet.

characters.name: Adam Groff
characters.line: Poured his heart into a poem for Eric and finally came out to his mother, only for Eric to end it anyway.

characters.name: Ruby Matthews
characters.line: Publicly dumped Otis after he couldn't say I love you; back to her queen bee position at school.

characters.name: Aimee Gibbs
characters.line: Slowly recovering from her bus assault through Jean's therapy; still struggling to be intimate with her boyfriend Steve.

characters.name: Cal Bowman
characters.line: Newly arrived non-binary student who has repeatedly clashed with Hope over uniform and gender rules.

characters.name: Isaac Goodwin
characters.line: Living close to Maeve, finally forgiven for the voicemail; briefly dated her before she chose Otis.

characters.name: Jackson Marchetti
characters.line: Demoted as head boy by Hope; befriended Cal but parted amicably after failing to understand their non-binary identity.

beats.label: S3 · Cavendish
beats.text: The Moordale students transfer to inclusive Cavendish College while Maeve stays in America, and she and Otis strain to make their long-distance relationship work.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cavendish is the new physical setting and the long-distance strain is Otis's entire arc.

beats.label: S3 · The rival
beats.text: Otis discovers Cavendish already has a popular student therapist, 'O', and they agree to hold an election to decide which clinic survives.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Otis vs O rivalry is the season's structural spine and shapes Ruby's re-entry.

beats.label: S3 · Otis and Ruby
beats.text: Otis sleeps with Ruby one night at her house while working on his campaign, then ignores her until she quits as his manager and ends the friendship in tears.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Their affair permanently changes Ruby and how she relates to Otis after he fails her again.

beats.label: S3 · Erin dies
beats.text: Maeve is called home when Erin overdoses; her mother dies, and at the funeral her estranged brother Sean gives a bitter eulogy and disappears again.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Erin's death removes Maeve's family anchor and clears the path for her America decision.

beats.label: S3 · O is Sarah
beats.text: O is unmasked as Sarah, the girl who bullied Ruby at summer camp; Ruby's old bed-wetting video is leaked, and O apologises publicly, revealing she is asexual.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The reveal collapses the season-long enmity and explains Ruby's lasting damage from it.

beats.label: S3 · One night
beats.text: Otis and Maeve reunite, sleep together and confess love, but she decides to return to America indefinitely to pursue a writing career.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the central relationship as mutually loved yet geographically split, unresolved for the next season.

beats.label: S3 · The reset
beats.text: Adam comes out as bisexual, Eric leaves his church over its rejection, Aimee finally kisses Isaac, and Otis makes peace with Jean after his heartbreak.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Every supporting character resets into a new starting position for the next season.

cliffhanger.text: Maeve has flown back to America to write and she and Otis have agreed to suspend contact entirely. Everyone has scattered from Cavendish's ordered world into decisions — coming out, leaving the church, kissing Isaac — that are still fresh.
questions: Can Otis and Maeve really suspend contact indefinitely and survive it?
Now that Ruby has ended their friendship for good, is that door truly closed?
What did Maeve write in the note she left behind for Otis?

characters.name: Otis Milburn
characters.line: Heartbroken as Maeve returns to America; reconciled with Jean and back on speaking terms with Eric.

characters.name: Maeve Wiley
characters.line: Back in America pursuing a writing career; slept with and confessed love to Otis before choosing to leave again.

characters.name: Eric Effiong
characters.line: Left his church after realising it will never accept him; single since breaking up with Adam.

characters.name: Jean Milburn
characters.line: Single mother of baby Joy, back on her radio show, with her chaotic sister Joanna staying with her.

characters.name: Ruby Matthews
characters.line: Slept with Otis, opened up, was rejected again; ended their friendship and returned to the Coven at Cavendish.

characters.name: Adam Groff
characters.line: Came out as bisexual and accepted his parents' reconciliation; asked out by his equestrian classmate Jem.

characters.name: Aimee Gibbs
characters.line: Found her voice through art and finally kissed Isaac, with Maeve's blessing to pursue him.

characters.name: Isaac Goodwin
characters.line: Now studying at Cavendish; recently confessed feelings with Aimee after Maeve released them both from the triangle.

characters.name: O / Sarah Owen
characters.line: Otis's rival therapist, exposed as Ruby's childhood bully; publicly apologised and disclosed she is asexual.

characters.name: Cal Bowman
characters.line: Non-binary student who ran away in crisis before Eric and Jackson convinced them they are wanted here.
